articles.title: Día de los Muertos Celebrations Underway in Albuquerque
articles.summary: A garland-making workshop led by Aleja Grajeda is part of the festivities in Old Town as people prepare for Día de los Muertos.
articles.content: As the holiday season approaches, many communities around the world are preparing for Día de los Muertos, a celebration that honors and remembers loved ones who have passed away. The festive atmosphere is palpable in Albuquerque's Old Town, where locals and visitors alike are busy decorating ofrendas with vibrant flowers, candles, and photographs. In a small store nestled in the heart of Old Town, a group of people gathered for a garland-making workshop led by Aleja Grajeda, owner of Las Ofrendas, a business that offers postpartum care, folk medicine, and other services. The room was filled with the sweet scent of copal incense and fresh flowers, creating a serene ambiance that seemed to welcome the spirits. As the participants worked on their garlands, they were surrounded by an assortment of materials, including photos of loved ones, plastic monarch butterflies, and candles. A child's note to a grandmother sat in a frame on one side of the room, adding a touch of warmth and intimacy to the space. The workshop was just one of many activities taking place in Albuquerque as people prepare for Día de los Muertos. This celebration is deeply rooted in Mexican culture and is traditionally observed from October 31 to November 2. During this time, it's believed that the dead can return to their family homes, and the living leave offerings to guide them on their journey. As the workshop participants worked on their garlands, they were given a special task: adding marigolds to complete their creations. These vibrant flowers have been associated with Día de los Muertos for centuries, and their sweet scent is said to help guide deceased ancestors back to their family homes. The store owner brought in a fresh batch of marigolds, which were added to the garlands as the final touch. The bright petals of these flowers add a pop of color to the festive decorations, making them an integral part of the celebration's visual appeal. Marigolds have been used for centuries in various cultures and traditions to ward off evil spirits and guide the dead on their journey. In the context of Día de los Muertos, they play a significant role in helping deceased ancestors find their way back to their loved ones. The significance of marigolds in Día de los Muertos is deeply rooted in their fragrance and appearance. The sweet scent of these flowers is believed to guide the dead on their return journey, while their bright petals add a festive touch to the celebrations. As the workshop came to an end, the participants had completed beautiful garlands adorned with marigolds, candles, and photographs. These delicate creations would soon be placed in homes and public spaces throughout Albuquerque, serving as a reminder of the love and respect that people have for their departed loved ones. The vibrant marigold, often seen in traditional Día de los Muertos celebrations, has its roots in ancient traditions and folklore. In the indigenous language Nahuatl, marigolds are referred to as cempasúchil, which translates to "the flower of 20 petals". This name is a testament to the intricate beauty of these flowers, with their layered petals resembling the complexity of traditional stories and legends. Before Spanish colonization, the Aztecs worshipped a goddess of death named Mictēcacihuātl. Her image was that of a skeleton's face, and she was revered during July and August. Despite the Catholic church's efforts to suppress this worship, it persisted among the Indigenous population. As time passed, people began incorporating their traditional ways of honoring the dead into the Catholic holidays of All Saints' Day and All Souls' Day. This blending of traditions eventually led to the evolution of Día de los Muertos. One of the enduring customs that survived this cultural fusion was the use of marigolds and other flowers to aid the dead on their journey home. These bright orange blooms have been imbued with a range of legends and symbolism. In many cultures, it's believed that marigolds possess the power to guide spirits back to their loved ones. Their strong scent is said to help navigate the soul through the afterlife. The use of flowers in Día de los Muertos celebrations is also deeply rooted in the idea of welcoming the dead into one's home and community. By placing marigolds in public spaces, people are able to honor and respect their departed loved ones. Marigolds have become an integral part of Día de los Muertos festivities, symbolizing love, remembrance, and the connection between the living and the dead. In this way, the humble marigold has transcended its status as a simple flower, becoming a powerful and enduring symbol of cultural heritage. The cultural significance of marigolds in Mexico's Día de los Muertos celebrations is deeply rooted in ancient mythology. One legend tells the story of Tonatiuh, the sun god, who gifted the people with these vibrant flowers to honor their loved ones who have passed away. In another tale, a couple named Xóchitl and Huitzilin are said to have been separated by death, but their love was so strong that it was transformed into a marigold flower. As long as this flower blooms, the couple's love is believed to endure, making marigolds a powerful symbol of eternal devotion. The story goes that Tonatiuh turned Xóchitl into a cempasúchil flower, which remained closed until Huitzilin's spirit returned in the form of a hummingbird. When the flower finally unfurled, its vibrant orange color was revealed to the world, signifying the reunion of the star-crossed lovers. Today, marigolds play a central role in many Día de los Muertos festivities, where they are often used to create elaborate displays and arrangements. In Mexican culture, scents are believed to guide the spirits of the dead back to the land of the living, making marigold petals particularly significant during this time. Marigolds are commonly displayed on ofrendas, in cemeteries, and as garlands, their sweet fragrance filling the air and helping to facilitate the reunion of loved ones. The marigold's layered petals hold significant meaning during Día de los Muertos celebrations. According to traditional interpretations, the multiple layers represent family and the generations that support one another. Each layer of petals also symbolizes love, with the new, delicate petals representing fresh emotions and the older, fading petals signifying past relationships. This dual representation highlights the importance of honoring both the living and the deceased. As part of a Día de los Muertos celebration, marigold garlands are often created to adorn homes and altars. These fragrant flowers are used in various ways, from decorating ofrendas to adorning cemeteries with their vibrant colors. To make these garlands, participants typically start by sipping traditional Mexican chocolate, a beverage that dates back to Mesoamerican civilizations. This rich drink is flavored with chile peppers, a staple ingredient in New Mexican cuisine. The warm and spicy flavors of the chocolate help set the tone for the garland-making process. As participants work on threading marigolds onto strings, they are reminded that their efforts will be appreciated by those who have passed on. During Día de los Muertos, food is left out to welcome ancestors returning from the spirit realm. This gesture acknowledges the long journey these spirits undertake and shows respect for their return. The process of making garlands involves threading marigolds onto strings alongside other flowers like purple blooms and orange slices. These colorful additions create a vibrant display that communicates celebration and hospitality. Baby's breath is another flower often used in Día de los Muertos arrangements, as it pays tribute to children who have passed away. The delicate white petals complement the bright colors of the marigolds and oranges, creating a harmonious visual display. As participants work on their garlands, they are encouraged by the thought that these colorful creations will welcome spirits returning from the afterlife with open arms. Marigolds are an integral part of Día de los Muertos celebrations in Mexico, but their use is not unique to this holiday. Many cultures around the world have a tradition of honoring the dead and celebrating their return from the afterlife. In Celtic cosmology, the time between late October and early November is believed to be a period when the veil between the living and the dead is at its thinnest. This idea is also reflected in European traditions such as Samhain, which was once celebrated with bonfires and the carving of faces into turnips. While these ancient holidays may have been suppressed or replaced by modern celebrations, their legacy lives on in many contemporary customs. Grajeda notes that people around the world have always found ways to honor their dead and connect with loved ones who have passed away. This universal desire to communicate with those beyond the grave is a common thread that runs through many cultures and traditions. Whether it's through elaborate ceremonies or simple gestures, people from all walks of life are drawn to the idea of bridging the gap between life and death. In this context, Día de los Muertos can be seen as just one part of a larger tapestry of human experience. It's a celebration that is open to interpretation and participation, inviting individuals to find their own way to honor their loved ones. While marigolds are an important element in Mexican Día de los Muertos celebrations, they are not the only flowers used during this time. Baby's breath, with its delicate white blooms, is also associated with the holiday and serves as a tribute to children who have passed away. The use of multiple colors and textures in garlands and other decorations adds depth and meaning to Día de los Muertos celebrations. By combining vibrant hues like yellowish-orange, purple, and gold, participants create a visual representation of welcome and celebration that is both beautiful and powerful. Ultimately, the true spirit of Día de los Muertos lies not in its specific traditions or rituals but in the universal desire to connect with those who have come before us. Whether through food, flowers, or other gestures, people from all over the world are drawn to this holiday as a way to honor their loved ones and celebrate the cycle of life. The connection between Día de los Muertos and Halloween is more than just a coincidence. The ancient Celtic holiday of Samhain, which marked the end of the harvest season and the beginning of winter, was also a time to honor the dead. Like the marigolds used during Día de los Muertos, some traditions from Samhain have persisted and evolved over time. Despite efforts to suppress it, the holiday's reverential roots continue to influence modern-day celebrations. articles.title: Chinese Spaceplane Resembles US X-37B Design
articles.summary: A commercial imaging satellite has captured high-resolution images of China's top-secret spaceplane, revealing similarities with the US Space Force's X-37B.
articles.content: A top-secret Chinese spaceplane has been spotted by a commercial imaging satellite, revealing details about its design that closely resemble those of the US Space Force's X-37B spaceplane. The spaceplane, which has delta wings and a payload bay door, bears an uncanny resemblance to its American counterpart. Its dark heat shield and rear-mounted service module with solar arrays further confirm the similarities between the two vehicles. This suggests that China may have studied or even copied aspects of the X-37B's design. The image was captured by Maxar, a company that provides reconnaissance imagery to the US military and intelligence agencies. The satellite's high-resolution view offers a rare glimpse into the Chinese spaceplane's features, which were previously only visible in lower-resolution images. The Pentagon has confirmed that the image is real, releasing it as part of an unclassified report by the Defense Intelligence Agency on threats to the United States in space. However, the report does not reveal any new information about what the spaceplane is used for or its capabilities. China's space program has been ramping up in recent years, with four spaceplane missions launched since 2020. The latest mission, which launched in February, remains in orbit today and has a duration of around nine months. The Chinese spaceplane is shrouded in secrecy, and it's unclear whether there's one or multiple units in service. In contrast, the US Space Force has two X-37B vehicles that have been used on eight missions to date, with the longest-running mission lasting nearly two-and-a-half years from launch to landing. Details about the X-37B's design and capabilities are publicly available, including photos released by US officials and information about its dimensions. However, most of its activities in space remain classified. China's spaceplane operates similarly to the X-37B, launching inside a rocket payload shroud before deploying as a satellite in orbit. A key advantage of spaceplanes like China's is their enhanced maneuverability, making them more suitable for certain missions than traditional satellites, according to a report from the Defense Intelligence Agency. China's spaceplane program has made significant strides in recent months, with the vehicle demonstrating its ability to catch objects in orbit. According to an analysis of open-source orbital tracking data, the Chinese spaceplane released a sub-satellite in June and successfully recaptured it in July. This feat was repeated in August and September, showcasing the spaceplane's capability for orbital maneuvers and object capture. The demonstration highlights the advanced technology behind China's spaceplane program, which has been shrouded in secrecy. The official name of the Chinese spaceplane remains a mystery, with Western publications referring to it as Shenlong based on reports from the 2000s about China's development of a robotic spaceplane. In contrast, Chinese state media refer to the vehicle as Chongfu Shiyong Shiyan Hangtian Qi, or CSSHQ, meaning reusable experimental spacecraft. The Secure World Foundation has published a fact sheet detailing the terminology used by Chinese state media to describe the spaceplane. The foundation's document highlights the complexity of nomenclature surrounding China's space program and the challenges it poses for international observers. The development of advanced space capabilities by China's military is being closely monitored by international observers, who are seeking to understand the implications of these technologies for global security. China's pursuit of anti-satellite technology, also known as "counterspace" weapons, has been identified as a key area of concern. This includes the use of directed-energy weapons (DEWs), which can be used to permanently or temporarily disable a satellite. The potential applications of DEWs in space are varied and concerning. One possible use is to dazzle sensors on an adversary's satellite, rendering it unable to gather critical information. China has reportedly developed ground-based laser systems with varying power levels that can disrupt, degrade, or damage satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO). China has also been testing anti-satellite missiles and has demonstrated the capability to refuel a satellite in geosynchronous orbit, a feat no other country has achieved above LEO. This development marks an important milestone in China's space program and highlights its growing capabilities. In addition to these developments, China has tested a robotic arm that could be used to snag a spacecraft out of orbit, raising concerns about the potential for on-orbit capture and manipulation. The country is also operating a fleet of satellites called TJS that are capable of approaching foreign spacecraft. The United States has been making progress in overcoming limitations related to its inspector satellites in geosynchronous orbit. The US Space Force has recently acquired additional satellites that can be refueled, allowing for greater maneuverability and potentially expanding their capabilities. This development comes as the Pentagon has acknowledged fielding weapons in space, marking a significant milestone for the United States. According to Air Force Secretary Troy Meink, the country is now the first nation to openly possess orbital weapons. This move highlights the growing importance of space-based military assets. Russia is also actively pursuing its own orbital combat program, with ambitions that include deploying nuclear weapons in space. US intelligence officials have confirmed this intention, indicating a heightened level of competition between the two nations in space. articles.title: Amazon's stock price falls after disappointing earnings report
articles.summary: Amazon reported third-quarter revenue of $201.9 billion, slightly below expectations, with profit falling short at $20.7 billion.
articles.content: Amazon's stock price took a hit on Thursday as investors grew concerned about the e-commerce giant's massive spending on artificial intelligence (AI) data centers and weaker advertising performance. The company reported third-quarter revenue of $201.9 billion, slightly below expectations, and its profit fell short at $20.7 billion. This decline was attributed to gains made a year ago from Amazon's investment in AI company Anthropic. Despite this, Amazon Web Services (AWS), the cloud computing unit, continued to thrive, with sales rising 39.3% to $45.98 billion, exceeding Wall Street targets. The strong demand for AWS services, particularly those tied to AI, remains a key driver of growth. However, Amazon's relentless spending on AI infrastructure is starting to raise eyebrows among investors. The company has reaffirmed its expectations that capital expenditures will reach about $220 billion in 2026, with the majority allocated towards AI data centers. The performance of non-cloud businesses, including advertising and holiday-quarter operating profit, is also under scrutiny, having missed analyst expectations. Amazon's heavy spending on AI infrastructure has pushed its free cash flow into negative territory, a stark contrast to last year when it was $14.8 billion positive. Shares of Amazon initially plummeted by 5% in after-hours trading following the release of its latest earnings report. The tech giant's financials come on the heels of similar reports from Microsoft and Alphabet, the parent company of Google, which also showcased robust growth in their cloud units and substantial investments in AI infrastructure. This trend suggests that the demand for artificial intelligence compute remains extremely high, prompting companies to continue pouring significant amounts of money into this area. As one of the largest spenders on data center construction, Amazon has been shifting its focus towards building out AI hubs. The company's capital expenditures are expected to contribute significantly to a projected $700 billion total spent by hyperscalers like Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet, and Meta Platforms in 2026. Amazon's latest financial projections indicate that it anticipates sales ranging from $240 billion to $247 billion for the current quarter, with operating income predicted to fall between $28.5 billion and $33.5 billion. This lower-than-expected operating income range has raised some eyebrows among analysts who had initially forecasted higher numbers. The timing of Amazon's annual Prime Day event this year may also have had a bearing on its third-quarter results, as it was held in the second quarter instead of its usual slot in the third quarter. Amazon's cloud computing unit is facing increased pressure to demonstrate strong growth rates as a result of the AI boom, which has put the spotlight on its ability to keep pace with its peers. The company's reliance on Amazon Web Services (AWS) for AI compute is evident in the prospectus filed by Anthropic, a lab that plans to spend at least $110 billion on AWS services over the next decade. This commitment is part of Anthropic's broader plan to invest at least $389.9 billion in cloud computing with major players like Microsoft and Alphabet. Amazon has invested heavily in AI research through its investments in companies like Anthropic, committing around $18 billion to date, with a potential for an additional $15 billion. However, the company's growth rates have slowed down due to its early mover advantage in cloud computing. As Amazon enters its critical holiday quarter, which accounts for most of its yearly revenue, it is gearing up for e-commerce demand peaks by hiring 300,000 workers. The company has recently introduced a range of hardware products, including Alexa tablets and the Bee AI wearable, as part of its efforts to boost sales. Despite this hiring spree, Amazon is also undertaking significant job cuts in other areas, with around 250 positions eliminated in its devices and services division this week, following earlier layoffs in retail. The company had previously shed about 30,000 workers between late 2025 and early this year. Amazon has begun to shift its focus towards a more strategic approach to artificial intelligence (AI). This change in tack is evident in the company's decision to block Meta's AI assistant, Muse, from accessing its online store in September. By doing so, Amazon aims to protect its core business model, which relies heavily on human interaction and advertising revenue. In a bid to foster a more outcome-driven culture within its software engineering team, Amazon has issued an internal memo emphasizing the importance of embracing AI while prioritizing tangible results. The company is urging its engineers to focus on developing solutions that benefit from current AI tooling rather than simply generating code or consuming tokens. This approach reflects a growing recognition within the industry that AI should be leveraged as a means to drive business outcomes, not merely as an end in itself. By encouraging engineers to think critically about where AI can and cannot add value, Amazon is seeking to cultivate a more informed and adaptable workforce. This shift in mindset should ultimately help the company stay ahead of the curve in an increasingly competitive market, where innovation and strategic decision-making will be key drivers of success. articles.title: US Executive Caught Up in International Espionage Case Involving China's Government
articles.summary: The US government is investigating Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen and data center executive who works for Megaspeed, over allegations of funneling information to the Chinese government while facilitating the sale of advanced Nvidia chips.
articles.content: A top executive at Nvidia has been caught up in a high-stakes international espionage case involving China's government. The US government is reportedly investigating Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen and data center executive who works for Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that buys chips from Nvidia to power its data centers. Megaspeed's data centers sell computing services to several prominent Chinese AI labs, including Qwen AI maker Alibaba. Unbeknownst to Jensen Huang, the CEO of Nvidia, Alice Huang had developed a close relationship with him, which has raised suspicions about her true intentions. US intelligence agencies have been monitoring Huang's activities electronically. According to reports, officials discovered that Huang was allegedly funneling information to the Chinese government in Beijing while also facilitating the sale of advanced Nvidia chips to China. The transfer of these chips is believed to be a violation of US law, sparking an investigation into Megaspeed and its ties to the Chinese AI industry. Details about what specific information Alice Huang may have shared with China are scarce at this time. However, officials confirm that an ongoing investigation and surveillance of her activities are taking place. The full scope and potential value of the information she provided remain unclear. The US government's lack of warning to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang about the situation has raised eyebrows. Sources suggest that revealing the suspicion could have compromised the US investigation into Megaspeed, making it a delicate matter for officials handling the case. Nvidia's involvement in a suspected espionage case has sparked concerns about the use of AI technology in international trade and conflict. The company's interactions with its customers, including Megaspeed, are being scrutinized, but an Nvidia spokesperson says they are "not unusual or unexpected" given the CEO's frequent communication with thousands of customer executives every year. Nvidia maintains that it treats all its regional cloud customers equally, and that sensitive trade secrets are not shared with them. The company is confident that if the US government believed any individual was a threat to American industry, they would be informed accordingly. The incident highlights the increasing importance of AI technology in global trade, with many experts warning about the potential risks and consequences of its use. This concern is echoed by recent events, including the FBI's arrest of a Saudi Arabian national accused of planting a recording device at an OpenAI executive meeting. As major tech companies continue to invest heavily in AI infrastructure, concerns about the environmental impact and public backlash against data centers are growing. The high demand for advanced computer chips has led to increased costs for RAM and storage, which are being passed on to consumers by hardware manufacturers. The Biden administration's efforts to restrict China's access to advanced computer chips have been met with mixed results. The ban on sales of certain Nvidia chips to China was implemented in 2022, but the rules were relaxed by President Trump in 2025. As a result of these relaxed regulations, the US government now receives 15% of revenue from Nvidia and AMD for chip sales to China. However, reports indicate that some unauthorized activities are still taking place, involving the smuggling of banned chips from the US to China. The investigation into this matter has been ongoing, with The Times reporting that Trump was briefed on the case a year ago but chose not to take any action, despite his close ties to Big Tech leaders like Jensen Huang.
